outputs.exact_statement: Let $A$ be a separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients. The following conditions are equivalent:* 1. *$\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A)<\infty$;* 2. *$A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$;* 3. *$\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A)\le1$.

Under the hypotheses of Theorem [thm:main], let $\iota_A:A\to A\otimes\mathcal Z$ be $\iota_A(a)=a\otimes1_\mathcal Z$. The conditions of that theorem are also equivalent to each of the following:* 1. *the canonical map $\mathrm{Cu}(\iota_A):\mathrm{Cu}(A)\to\mathrm{Cu}(A\otimes\mathcal Z)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf{Cu}$;* 2. *there is an abstract isomorphism $\mathrm{Cu}(A)\cong\mathrm{Cu}(A\otimes\mathcal Z)$ in $\mathbf{Cu}$.* *The abstract isomorphism need not be induced by a $*$-homomorphism.
For every separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra $A_0$, $$\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A_0\otimes\mathcal Z)\le1.$$
For every nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra $D$ with no characters, there is a finite integer $n\ge1$ such that $D^{\otimes_{\max}n}$ contains two full orthogonal positive elements.

For every separable nuclear $D$ there are finite-dimensional algebras $F_n$ and c.p.c. maps $$D\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}D$$ such that $\beta_n\alpha_n\to\mathrm{id}_D$ in point-norm, $\|\alpha_n(a)\alpha_n(b)\|\to0$ for orthogonal $a,b\in D_+$, and each $\beta_n$ is a finite convex combination of c.p.c. order-zero maps $F_n\to D$.
If $v\in D_+$ is full and $D$ is unital, then there are $y_1,\ldots,y_N\in D$ such that $$\sum_{l=1}^N y_l^*vy_l=1_D.$$

If $D\cong D\otimes\mathcal Z$, then $W(D)$ is almost unperforated. More generally, if $W(D)$ is almost unperforated, $u,v\in D_+$, $u\in\operatorname{Ideal}_D(v)$, and $$d([u])<d([v])\quad\text{for every dimension function $d$ with }d([v])=1,$$ then $u\precsim v$.

Let $D$ be exact and $\mathcal Z$-stable. If $u,v\in D_+$ satisfy $$d_\tau(u)\le\tfrac12d_\tau(v)
 \quad\text{for every lower semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ on $D$},$$ then $u\precsim v$.

Let $A$ be unital, let $k\ge1$, and let $\lambda$ be a lower semicontinuous extended trace on $A\otimes M_k$. Set $\tau(a)=\lambda(a\otimes1_k)$ and $L_k=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\operatorname{tr}_k$, with normalized matrix trace. Then $$\lambda(z)=\tau(L_k(z))\qquad(z\in(A\otimes M_k)_+).$$ No finiteness assumption on $\lambda$ is needed.

Let $X_n$ be nonempty sets and let $f_{j,n}:X_n\to[0,\infty)$ be given for $j,n\in\mathbb N$. Suppose that for every $m$ and $\delta>0$ there is $(x_n)\in\prod_nX_n$ with $\lim_{n\to\omega}f_{j,n}(x_n)<\delta$ for $1\le j\le m$. Then there is a single $(x_n)$ for which all these ultralimits are zero.

Let $u,y\in D_+$ and $0\le a<b$. If $u\precsim(y-b)_+$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $r\in D$ such that $$\|u-r^*(y-a)_+r\|<\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \|r\|^2\le\frac{\|u\|+\varepsilon}{b-a}.$$ Here $(y-0)_+=y$. In particular the bound is uniform in a family of contractions $u$ with a common gap $b-a>0$.

Let $D$ be exact and let $\Phi,\Psi:D\to E$ be nuclear completely positive maps, with $\Psi$ of order zero. Suppose $$\Phi(a)\in\operatorname{Ideal}_E(\Psi(a))\qquad(a\in D_+).$$ For every finite $\mathcal F\subset D$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are $y_1,\ldots,y_N\in E$ such that $$\left\|\Phi(a)-\sum_{l=1}^Ny_l^*\Psi(a)y_l\right\|<\varepsilon
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal F).$$

Let $D_n$ be separable unital $\mathcal Z$-stable algebras, put $D_\omega=\prod_\omega D_n$, and let $A$ be separable and unital. For a c.p.c. order-zero map $\rho:A\to D_\omega$ set $$C=D_\omega\cap\rho(A)'\cap\{1-\rho(1)\}^{\perp}.$$ Assume that $C$ is full in $D_\omega$ and that every full hereditary subalgebra $E\subset C$ has the following property: whenever $x\in E$ admits totally full $e_l,e_r\in E_+$ with $e_lx=xe_r=0$, there is a full $s\in E$ satisfying $sx=xs=0$. If $h_0,h_1\in C_+$ are totally full contractions and $$f(h_0)\sim f(h_1)\quad\text{in }C
 \qquad\text{for every }f\in C_0((0,1])_+,$$ then $uh_1u^*=h_0$ for some unitary $u\in\widetilde C$.

There are finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras $F_n$, powers $k_n$ of $2$, and completely positive contractive maps $$A\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n \xrightarrow{\beta_n}A\otimes M_{k_n}, \qquad \theta_n=\beta_n\alpha_n,$$ with the following properties.* 1. *Each $\beta_n$ has order zero, and $$\|\alpha_n(c)\alpha_n(d)\|\longrightarrow0 \quad(c,d\in A_+,\ cd=0).$$* 2. *For every $a\in A$, $$\|L_{k_n}(\theta_n(a))-a\|\longrightarrow0.$$* 3. *For every $n,j\geq1$ there is a positive contraction $w_{n,j}\in A\otimes M_{k_n}$, and there are nonnegative numbers $\eta_{n,j},\delta_{n,j}$ tending to zero as $n\to\infty$ for each fixed $j$, such that $$\begin{aligned} \|w_{n,j}-\theta_n(x_j)\|&\leq\eta_{n,j}, \label{model:retained-norm}\\ \tau(L_{k_n}(w_{n,j})) &\leq \tau(x_j)+\delta_{n,j}d_\tau(b_j) \label{model:retained-trace} \end{aligned}$$ for every lower semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ on $A$ with $d_\tau(b_j)<\infty$.* *The coefficients in [model:retained-trace] are independent of $\tau$. One may take $\delta_{n,j}=2^{-n}$ for all $n,j$.

Fix $m\geq1$, a finite subset $\mathcal F$ of the unit ball of $A$, a finite family $\mathcal O$ of pairs of orthogonal positive contractions in $A$, and $\varepsilon>0$. There are a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra $F$, a power $k$ of $2$, completely positive contractive maps $$A\xrightarrow{\alpha}F\xrightarrow{\beta}A\otimes M_k,
 \qquad\theta=\beta\alpha,$$ and positive contractions $w_1,\ldots,w_m\in A\otimes M_k$ such that $\beta$ has order zero and $$\begin{aligned}
 \|L_k(\theta(a))-a\|&<\varepsilon
       &&(a\in\mathcal F), \label{model:finite-approx}\\
 \|\alpha(c)\alpha(d)\|&<\varepsilon
       &&((c,d)\in\mathcal O), \label{model:finite-orth}\\
 \|w_j-\theta(x_j)\|&<\varepsilon
       &&(1\leq j\leq m), \label{model:finite-retained}\\
 \tau(L_k(w_j))&\leq\tau(x_j)+\varepsilon d_\tau(b_j)
       &&(1\leq j\leq m, d_\tau(b_j)<\infty).
       \label{model:finite-trace}
\end{aligned}$$ The last inequality holds for every lower semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ satisfying the indicated finite-rank condition.

The composites $\theta_n$ also asymptotically preserve orthogonality. Indeed, the order-zero product estimate gives $$\|\theta_n(c)\theta_n(d)\|
 \leq\|\alpha_n(c)\alpha_n(d)\|
 \qquad(c,d\in A_+).$$ Consequently they induce a c.p.c. order-zero map into $\prod_n(A\otimes M_{k_n})/\bigoplus_n(A\otimes M_{k_n})$, and into the corresponding norm ultraproduct. The same conclusion holds after composing the $\beta_n$ with any c.p.c. order-zero maps into a fixed target algebra: the displayed product estimate remains valid for each composite return map.

For every integer $k\geq 1$ and every $\xi>0$ there is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\iota\colon M_k\to\mathcal Z$ such that $$\tau_{\mathcal Z}(\iota(1))>1-\xi,
 \qquad \|\iota(e_{11})\|=1.$$

For every integer $m\geq2$ there are a positive contraction $D_m\in\mathcal Z$ of norm one, contractions $v_{m,1},\ldots,v_{m,m}\in\mathcal Z$, and a finite positive integer $K_m$ such that $$\label{supplies:copy-relations}
 v_{m,r}^*v_{m,s}=\delta_{rs}D_m,
 \qquad
 1=\sum_{l=1}^{K_m}y_{m,l}^*(D_m-1/2)_+y_{m,l}$$ for suitable $y_{m,l}\in\mathcal Z$.

There is a positive contraction $e\in B_1$ such that, with $q=1-e$, $$\label{setup:common-equations}
 L(e)=0,\qquad
 [e,\pi(a)]=[e,\theta(a)]=0,\qquad
 q\theta(a)=q\pi(a)
 \quad(a\in A).$$ In particular, if $h=\theta(1)$, then $qh=q$.

There is a sequence $m(n)\geq2$ with $m(n)\to_\omega\infty$ such that, on putting $$P_n=D_{m(n)}\in\mathcal Z_2,\qquad P=(P_n)_\omega\in B,
 \qquad
 \Psi(a)=P(q-1/2)_+\pi(a),$$ the map $\Psi\colon A\to B$ is c.p.c. order zero and, for every $j\geq1$, $$\label{trace:small-part-comparison}
 e\pi(x_j),\ e\theta(x_j)
 \precsim (\Psi(a_j)-c_j)_+
 \quad\text{in }B,
 \qquad c_j=\gamma_j/64.$$

For every positive integer $L$ there are contractions $v_1,\ldots,v_L\in B$, represented entirely in the $\mathcal Z_2$ leg, such that $$\label{trace:ultrapower-copies}
 v_l^*v_{l'}=\delta_{ll'}P\qquad(1\leq l,l'\leq L).$$ In particular these elements commute with $B_1$, and hence with $\pi(A)$ and $q$.

There is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\widehat\theta\colon A\to B$ whose range commutes with the constant copy of $\mathcal Z_3$ and such that $$\begin{aligned}
 h\widehat\theta(a)=\widehat\theta(a)h&=\theta(a),
       \qquad a\in A,\label{support:factorization}\\
 [e,\widehat\theta(a)]&=0,
 \qquad q\widehat\theta(a)=q\pi(a),\qquad a\in A,
       \label{support:common}\\
 e\widehat\theta(a'),\ e\pi(a')&\in\operatorname{Ideal}_B(\Psi(a')),
       \qquad a'\in A_+.
       \label{support:ideals}
\end{aligned}$$
The elements $Q_0,Q_1$ and $H$ are full in $C$, and $C$ is full in $M_2(B)$.
The ordered semigroup $W(C)$ is almost unperforated.

Let $D\subset C$ be a full hereditary subalgebra. Suppose that $y\in D$ and that totally full positive elements $e_l,e_r\in D$ satisfy $$e_l y=ye_r=0.$$ Then there is a full element $s\in D$ with $sy=ys=0$.
The elements $h_0,h_1$ are totally full in $C$. For every $g\in C_0((0,1])_+$, the elements $g(h_0)$ and $g(h_1)$ are Cuntz equivalent in $C$.

Put $k^{[0]}=k$ and $k^{[1]}=1-k$, in the constant third leg. There are unitaries $U_0,U_1\in M_2(B)$ such that $$\label{conjugacy:weighted-equation}
 U_i\bigl(k^{[i]}\theta(a)\bigr)^{(1)}U_i^*
   =\bigl(k^{[i]}\pi(a)\bigr)^{(0)},
 \qquad a\in A,\quad i=0,1.$$ They can be chosen to commute with $\rho(A)$.

Let $A$ be a nonzero separable unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra and put $R=A\otimes\mathcal Z^{\otimes3}$. For every finite $\mathcal F\subset A$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the map $$\kappa_A:A\longrightarrow M_2(R),\qquad
 \kappa_A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a\otimes1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$$ admits a finite-dimensional approximation with two colours: there are a finite-dimensional algebra $F$, a c.p.c. map $\alpha:A\to F$, and c.p.c. order-zero maps $\varphi_0,\varphi_1:F\to M_2(R)$ such that $$\|\varphi_0\alpha(a)+\varphi_1\alpha(a)-\kappa_A(a)\|
 <\varepsilon\qquad(a\in\mathcal F).$$

To pass from the corner inclusion to the algebra itself, we first amplify by finite matrices. Matrix amplification preserves each order-zero return map, and the stabilization accommodates the second diagonal block of the amplified target. The resulting approximations still have two colours.

Let $A$ be unital. Suppose that the first-corner inclusion $A\to M_2(A)$ has finite-dimensional approximations with two colours, with a c.p.c. first map and c.p.c. order-zero return maps. Then $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A\otimes\mathcal K)\le1$.

Fix $k\geq2$ and $0<r<1$. There are $n\geq1$ and $G\in(\mathbb R^k)^{\otimes n}$ such that, for every list of pairs of unit vectors $(u_j^0,u_j^1)_{j=1}^n$ satisfying $$|\langle u_j^0,u_j^1\rangle|\leq r\qquad(1\leq j\leq n),$$ the numbers $$\big\langle G,u_1^{\alpha_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n^{\alpha_n}\big\rangle,
 \qquad \alpha\in\{0,1\}^n,$$ include a value greater than $1/2$ and a value less than $-1/2$.
Let $M_1,\ldots,M_n\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be mutually commuting unital von Neumann factors. If $e_j\in M_j$ is positive and $\|e_j\|=1$, then $$\left\|\prod_{j=1}^ne_j\right\|=1.$$

Let $E$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra and $\rho$ a pure state. Given a finite set $\mathcal F\subset E$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a positive contraction $f\in E$ with $\|f\|=1$ such that $$\|fxf-\rho(x)f^2\|<\varepsilon\qquad(x\in\mathcal F).$$

Let $A\ne0$ be separable with $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}A\leq d<\infty$.*

1.  *If no hereditary subalgebra of $A$ has a finite-dimensional irreducible representation, then there are finitely many finite-dimensional algebras $E_j$, completely positive order-zero maps $\varphi_j:E_j\to F(A)$, and elements $c_j\in F(A)$ such that every matrix summand of every $E_j$ has size at least two and $$1_{F(A)}=\sum_jc_j^*\varphi_j(1_{E_j})c_j.$$ This is the matrix-threshold-two consequence of the covering-number bound $\operatorname{cov}(F(A))\le(d+1)^2$ [[WZNuclear](#ref-WZNuclear), Definition 4.1 and Proposition 4.3].*

2.  *If $F(A)$ contains two full orthogonal positive elements, then $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\mathcal Z$ [[RT](#ref-RT), Theorem 1.2].*

*Both assertions apply to nonunital $A$, with the annihilator quotient just defined.
If $A\ne0$ is separable, nowhere scattered, and has finite nuclear dimension, then $F(A)$ has no characters.

Let $A\ne0$ be separable, and let $D\subseteq F(A)$ be a separable unital subalgebra with the same unit. For every finite $n$, there is a unital $*$-homomorphism $$D^{\otimes_{\max}n}\longrightarrow F(A).$$

The same argument proves that $F(A)$ has two full orthogonal positive elements whenever $A\ne0$ is separable and $F(A)$ has no characters. Finite nuclear dimension enters the proof of Theorem [thm:main] only through the two imported results in Theorem 39.
